name: Jardim Zoológico de Lisboa (Lisbon Zoo)
seoTitle: Lisbon Zoo on a Cruise Stop: Who It Suits and Timing
tagline: A large city zoo one metro ride from the ship, worth a port day mainly for families with young children

description.short: Lisbon's zoo, founded in 1884 and on its current Sete Rios site since 1905, with about 2,000 animals of around 300 species. It is a direct Blue Line metro ride from Santa Apolónia; adult entry is €31.
description.full:
For most cruise passengers the zoo is a weak use of a day in Lisbon. It costs €31 per adult, needs three hours or more to be worthwhile, and shows little of the city. It does make sense for families with young children who have had enough of monuments and hills, for repeat visitors, or on a long call when the children's day matters more than sightseeing.

Getting there is easy. Walk about 10 minutes from the terminal to Santa Apolónia and take the metro Blue Line direct to Jardim Zoológico, roughly 20 minutes with no change; the zoo entrance is beside the station. A taxi takes about 20 minutes.

Inside, the timed presentations shape the visit. From 21 September to 20 March the dolphin presentation runs at 11:00 (not on Tuesdays) and 14:30 and lasts 20 minutes; the bird presentation at the Bosque Encantado runs at 12:30 and 16:00 all year. Arriving at 10:00 and heading for the 11:00 dolphins, then the bird show at 12:30, covers the highlights by early afternoon. The zoo's own cable car, included in the ticket, gives a 20-minute ride over the park, but it does not run in rain or strong wind and cannot take wheelchairs or pushchairs. The small Zoo train is extra (€1 adults, €0.50 children) and runs Wednesday to Sunday only.

The ticket offices close at 17:15 in winter and 18:45 in summer. Weekends and school holidays are the busiest times; weekday mornings are quieter. Buying online saves 5 per cent. Children under 13 must be accompanied by an adult over 18, and guide dogs are not admitted.

If your group is mixed, the Oceanário is the more compact family alternative and is entirely indoors.
description.history: The zoo opened in 1884 as the first park of its kind in the Iberian Peninsula, founded by Pedro Van der Laan, José Tomás de Sousa Martins and the Baron of Kessler with the support of King Fernando II and the zoologist José Vicente Barbosa du Bocage. It began in the Parque de São Sebastião da Pedreira, moved to Palhavã, and on 28 May 1905 opened on its permanent site at the Quinta das Laranjeiras in Sete Rios. After 1974 the loss of state support and of animal shipments from the former colonies hit it hard, and from 1990 a new management modernised the enclosures, opening a veterinary hospital in 2008.
description.significance: It is one of the older zoos still operating in Europe, with about 2,000 animals of roughly 300 species, and a member of the European and world zoo associations, EAZA and WAZA. Its 2008 veterinary hospital was singled out by EAZA as the best in Europe. For visitors, its practical value is that it is the one big outdoor family attraction reachable by a single metro line from the ship.

directions.general: Located in Sete Rios, northwest of central Lisbon, near Benfica neighborhood
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7.8 km from the terminal, not walkable. Metro Blue Line runs direct from Santa Apolónia (10 minutes' walk from the terminal) to Jardim Zoológico station, about 20 minutes, with the zoo entrance next to the exit. Taxi about 20 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro: Blue Line to Jardim Zoológico station (exit leads directly to zoo). Buses: 701, 716, 726, 746, 755, 758. Train: Sete Rios station (5-minute walk).
directions.parking: Paid parking available at zoo entrance and nearby shopping centers

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open every day of the year

admissionPrices.notes: Prices from 1 January 2026: adults 13-64 €31; children 3-12 €19; seniors 65+ €22; children up to 2 free (ID required for reduced fares). 5% off when bought online (valid 120 days). Includes all presentations and the cable car; the Zoo train is extra (€1 adults, €0.50 children and seniors, Wednesday to Sunday). 30% off for visitors with a declared disability of 60% or more, at the ticket office only.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Weekday mornings at 10:00, timed for the 11:00 dolphin presentation (not on Tuesdays in winter).
busyPeriods: Presentation times at the Baía dos Golfinhos
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Check the presentation times on zoo.pt on the day, as they can change without notice. Bring sun protection in summer. Children under 13 need an adult over 18. Re-entry is allowed the same day until the ticket offices close.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 5 hours: 30 minutes each way from the ship plus 3-4 hours inside
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Metro Blue Line direct from Santa Apolónia (10 minutes' walk from the ship) to Jardim Zoológico, about 20 minutes. Inside, paved paths with some slopes.
combinableWith: Palácio dos Marqueses de Fronteira (check guided-visit times)
Oceanário de Lisboa (as an alternative, not on the same day)
tips: Take the metro Blue Line from Santa Apolónia straight to Jardim Zoológico, about 20 minutes with no change.
In winter the dolphin presentation is at 11:00 (not Tuesdays) and 14:30, and needs at least 30 spectators to go ahead.
The Bosque Encantado bird presentation runs at 12:30 and 16:00; it is cancelled in rain or strong wind.
Buy tickets online for 5 per cent off; tickets are valid for 120 days.
Adults pay €31, children 3-12 €19 and seniors 65+ €22; under-3s go free.
The included cable car runs 11:00-17:30 (last trip) in winter and 11:30-19:30 in summer, but not in rain or high wind.
The Zoo train costs extra (€1) and runs only Wednesday to Sunday.
Ticket offices close at 17:15 in winter and 18:45 in summer, so leave the ship by early afternoon at the latest.

highlights: Baía dos Golfinhos dolphin presentation (20 minutes)
Bosque Encantado bird presentation at 12:30 and 16:00
Vale dos Tigres with Sumatran tigers
Savana MEO with elephants, giraffes and lions
Quintinha do Lidl farm area for young children
Cable car over the park, included in the ticket
facilities: Restaurants and cafés in the free-access area at the entrance, plus two snack bars inside
Picnic area in the Bosque Encantado
Two ATMs in the free-access area
Pushchair rental for children aged 3-10 (€7, €20 cash deposit)
Wheelchairs on request at the entrance, subject to availability

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Paths are paved but the park has slopes. Wheelchairs can be requested from security at the entrance (no reservations). The cable car and the Zoo train are not recommended for people with reduced mobility, and the cable car does not take wheelchairs or pushchairs. Guide dogs are not admitted.
